analysis: The only change to docs/reference/configuration.md is a single added table row (head line 330) documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED, a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel selector for the qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. It is a documentation-only change, so no code, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or wire behavior is altered here. The row says the variable is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents, so it adds no new passthrough into the installed daemon environment. Forced kernels (`packed` or `rows`) skip the bit-for-bit probe and are described as A/B measurement only. Because the setting is operator-local, it is within the operator-controlled environment already assumed by TB-003 and T-013. It does not touch the prefix cache (T-041), attestation (TB-009), App Attest (TB-011) or the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002). I found no threat-model assumption invalidated and no mitigation weakened. Remaining unverified contract: the referenced implementation in libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift is not in this batch, so I could not confirm that the documented behavior (stock kernel retained for decode, MTP verification and masked updates) matches the code. The head patch excerpt was truncated, and the base units end at line 486, so I could not confirm the rest of the file. This is a documentation-accuracy point, not a demonstrated security regression. Any numerical-divergence concern from a forced kernel relates to T-007-style output correctness only for operators who choose it themselves.
